gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Striking in its compressed rhythm, Expose barely pauses between lowercase and capitals. And Noto Sans Lisu answers that tension with generously opened s curves, so the whole pairing feels refined without ever getting fussy.
gen-fs-expose-poppins: Poppins carries sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase and loose curves that keep their width through every turn, under Expose's tight display lines. Compression above, openness below.
gen-fs-expose-rubik: Tightly packed and refined, Expose hardly leaves any gap between its small letters and capitals. But Rubik's soft, large lowercase and open round shapes give the pairing its strongest quality: a crisp, friendly counterweight.
gen-fs-gambarino-fs-roundo: Dramatic ink-heavy stems lead the way in Gambarino, with hairline tips. Roundo follows in geometric, even-handed lines, its horizontals as stout as its verticals, so paragraphs would move along smoothly without any flicker.
gen-fs-gambarino-gf-lexend-peta: Swollen curves tapering into hairline ends give Gambarino its drama, and Lexend Peta meets that with curves drawn like a technical pen. Its wide-mouthed c shapes make the strongest single quality here the sheer difference in stroke.
gen-fs-kola-fs-ranade: Bold and unfussy, Kola sets a moderate-height lowercase against Ranade, whose letters stand taller and sit wide apart with only a slight shift in weight. They fill the page together with a loose, organic ease.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-spline-sans: New Title packs its tall lowercase into tight, chain-like links that read bold and modern. Spline Sans opens up with wide gaps at its curve ends, and its matched strokes make the strongest contrast of the two.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-stack-sans-headline: Wiry, technical, and almost all capitals in feel. Nippo excels at sharp, cut-wire display lettering, while Stack Sans Headline keeps its monoline sans-serif forms crisp and open when the sizes get tiny.
gen-fs-oswald-bitter: Oswald stands tight and strong in its knitted rows. Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase and an open s, gives the pair its strongest quality: a sturdy, grounded heft that feels dependable.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-epilogue: Oswald packs its lines tight and confident. Epilogue loosens everything with curvy, wire-like monoline letters and a tall lowercase, which is where the pair gets its strongest quality: tension between compressed and open.
